prerequisites.title: Linear Transformations of Objects in the Plane

sections.markdown:
Consider the linear transformation $\mathbf{T}$ whose matrix $T$ is given by
$T=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 4 \\ 4 & 10\end{bmatrix}$
Suppose we know that some vector $\mathbf{v}$ in the plane is mapped to the vector $\mathbf w$ under the action of $\mathbf T,$ where the vector $\mathbf w$ is given by $$ \mathbf{w} = \begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 6\end{bmatrix}. $$ The mapping $\mathbf T(\mathbf v) = \mathbf w$ is shown schematically in the diagram below. ![](images/b5/b53ed555a52830fd0dcc0ba150c618fd8b527a0261c8e3caf09378c47dc6ffae.png) How can we find the original vector $\mathbf v?$ To find the vector $\mathbf v,$ we compute the inverse of the matrix $T$ and then use it to reverse the action of $\mathbf T.$ Let's see how this works. From the given information, we have $$ T\cdot \mathbf{v} = \begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 6\end{bmatrix}. $$ If we pre-multiply the above equation by $T^{-1},$ we get $$ \begin{aligned}{T}^{-1}\cdot T\cdot v & ={T}^{-1}\cdot \begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 6\end{bmatrix} \\ {I}_{2}\cdot v & ={T}^{-1}\cdot \begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 6\end{bmatrix} \\ v & ={T}^{-1}\cdot \begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 6\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned} $$ This equation tells that to find the vector $\mathbf v,$ we need to pre-multiply the vector $\mathbf w$ by the inverse of $T.$ So, we now calculate the inverse of $T\mathbin{:}$ $$ \begin{aligned}{T}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{20-16}\begin{bmatrix}10 & -4 \\ -4 & 2\end{bmatrix} \\ & =\frac{1}{4}\begin{bmatrix}10 & -4 \\ -4 & 2\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned} $$ Therefore, we can calculate the original vector $\mathbf v$ as follows: $$ \begin{aligned}v & ={T}^{-1}\cdot \begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 6\end{bmatrix} \\ & =\frac{1}{4}\begin{bmatrix}10 & -4 \\ -4 & 2\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 6\end{bmatrix} \\ & =\frac{1}{4}\begin{bmatrix}-4 \\ 4\end{bmatrix} \\ & =\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned} $$ We can easily check that this is the correct answer by computing $T\cdot \mathbf v\mathbin{:}$ $$ \begin{aligned}T\cdot v & =\begin{bmatrix}2 & 4 \\ 4 & 10\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 1\end{bmatrix} \\ & =\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 6\end{bmatrix}\,✓\end{aligned} $$ We summarize the process we just completed in the following diagram. ![](images/69/6991d3f7be5f29f51512ed927189ea10cbbcdb9dc6a2ce00573759201fb684a6.png) In general, if $T$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix that represents a linear transformation, then $T^{-1}$ is the inverse linear transformation and, if it exists, it reverses the action of $T.$ So for any vector $\mathbf{v}$ on the plane, we have $$ T^{-1}\cdot T\cdot \mathbf{v} = I_2 \cdot \mathbf{v} = \mathbf{v}. $$
sections.title: Introduction

knowledgePoint.title: Calculating a Vector Given Its Image Under a Linear Transformation

sections.markdown:
The vector $\mathbf{v}$ in the plane is mapped to the vector $\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 4\end{bmatrix}$ under the action of the linear transformation $\mathbf{T}$ whose matrix $T$ is given by
$$
T={\left[ \begin{array}{cc}5 & - 2 \\ 10 & - 3\end{array} \right]}.
$$
What is the original vector $\mathbf{v}?$
sections.title: Calculating a Vector Given Its Image Under a Linear Transformation
sections.workedSolution:
From the given information, we have

$$
T\cdot \mathbf{v} = {\left[ \begin{array}{c}1 \\ 4\end{array} \right]}.
$$

We need to reverse the action of the matrix $T.$ So, we multiply the above equation by $T^{-1},$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1}\cdot T\cdot v & ={T}^{-1}\cdot \begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 4\end{bmatrix} \\ v & ={T}^{-1}\cdot \begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 4\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to calculate the inverse of $T$, which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{-15-(-20)}\begin{bmatrix}-3 & 2 \\ -10 & 5\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\begin{bmatrix}-3 & 2 \\ -10 & 5\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the original vector is

$$
\begin{aligned}v & ={T}^{-1}\cdot \begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 4\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\begin{bmatrix}-3 & 2 \\ -10 & 5\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 4\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ 10\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

knowledgePoint.title: Calculating the Vertices of a Polygon Given Its Image Under a Linear Transformation

sections.markdown:
Consider the linear transformation $\mathbf T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by
$$
T = {\left[ \begin{array}{cc}4 & - 1 \\ 3 & 1\end{array} \right]}.
$$

The triangle $S$ is mapped to the triangle $S'$ under the action of $\mathbf T.$ The triangle $S'$ has vertices $(4,3),(4,10),$ and $(-4,-3).$ Which of the following are vertices of $S?$

- $(1,0)$

- $(4,-3)$

- $(-1,0)$
sections.title: Calculating the Vertices of a Polygon Given Its Image Under a Linear Transformation
sections.workedSolution:
First, we create a matrix $Y$ containing all of the vertices of $S'\mathbin{:}$ 

$$
Y = 
{\left[ \begin{array}{ccc}4 & 4 & - 4 \\ 3 & 10 & - 3\end{array} \right]}
$$

Now, if $X$ denotes the matrix that contains the corresponding vertices of $S$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}T\cdot X & =Y \\ T\cdot X & =\begin{bmatrix}4 & 4 & -4 \\ 3 & 10 & -3\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

We need to reverse the action of the matrix $T.$ So, we multiply the above equation by $T^{-1},$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1}\cdot T\cdot X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot \begin{bmatrix}4 & 4 & -4 \\ 3 & 10 & -3\end{bmatrix} \\ X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot \begin{bmatrix}4 & 4 & -4 \\ 3 & 10 & -3\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

The inverse of $T$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{4-(-3)}\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 \\ -3 & 4\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\frac{1}{7}\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 \\ -3 & 4\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot \begin{bmatrix}4 & 4 & -4 \\ 3 & 10 & -3\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\frac{1}{7}\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 \\ -3 & 4\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}4 & 4 & -4 \\ 3 & 10 & -3\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\frac{1}{7}\begin{bmatrix}7 & 14 & -7 \\ 0 & 28 & 0\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 4 & 0\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, the coordinates of the vertices of the original triangle are $(1,0),(2,4),(-1,0).$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."
